- **Tomorrow**: publish → tabulate → use AI honestly → present

## A folder you have seen

```
📁 Thesis final
   ├── data_final.xlsx
   ├── data_final_v2.xlsx
   ├── data_final_v2_USE THIS.xlsx
   ├── analysis.spv
   ├── Table1_edited_sir comments.docx
   └── Copy of data_final_v2_USE THIS (1).xlsx
```

. . .

**Which file produced Table 2?**

::: {.notes}
⏱️ 4 min. Show of hands: who recognises this folder? Everyone will laugh.
That laugh is the whole motivation for the workshop — use it.
:::

## This is not carelessness

It is what happens when the **record** of the analysis is separate from the
**doing** of it.

. . .

Clicks leave no trace.

::: {.notes}
Important framing: nobody in the room is being blamed. The workflow is at
fault, not the researcher.
:::

## Three words, three claims

| | Same data? | Same code? |
|---|---|---|
| **Reproducibility** | Yes | Yes |
| **Replicability** | No | Yes |
| **Generalisability** | No | No |

. . .

Only the first is entirely **within your control**.

::: {.notes}
⏱️ 6 min. Ask which one most people mean when they say "replicate". Usually
the wrong one. No funding, no new participants, no collaborators needed for
reproducibility — that is the selling point.
:::

## Reproducible ≠ correct

A reproducible analysis can be reproducibly wrong.

. . .

What it buys you is that the error is **findable**.

::: {.notes}
Head off the objection before it is raised. Someone always raises it.
:::

## The spectrum {.smaller}

```
Publication only → + Code → + Code & data → + Linked & executable → Replication
        ↑                                            ↑
   most med-ed papers                        where you will be
                                             by Thursday evening
```

::: {.notes}
Peng RD, Science 2011. Position the room honestly — most are at the far left,
and that is normal.
:::

## Where analyses break

::: {.incremental}
1. **The undocumented manual step** — "I removed the two who withdrew"
2. **The absolute path** — `C:/Users/Ananya/Desktop/final/data.csv`
3. **The stale environment** — works only in a warm session
:::

::: {.notes}
⏱️ 8 min. Ask for a show of hands on each. All three cost nothing to fix,
which is the point of the next slide.
:::

## The test

::: {.big-number}
Restart. Source. Compare.
:::

<kbd>Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + F10</kbd>, then run your script top to bottom.

If every number reappears, you are reproducible.

::: {.notes}
🎯 The single most portable idea in the session. Have them write it down.
:::

## What we ask you to change

::: {.incremental}
1. One project folder per study
2. A script for every number
3. Relative paths, always
4. A clean session, always
5. Version control — later, not this week
:::

. . .

Items 1–4 are free.

## Discussion — 5 minutes {background-color="#0f5257"}

In your groups:

1. Could you regenerate Table 1 of your last paper today?
2. Could a co-author?
3. Which failure point bites first?

::: {.notes}
⏱️ 5 min. Walk the room. Collect two honest answers to share aloud —
volunteering an embarrassing one yourself sets the tone.
:::

## Ground rules

- 45 min teaching, 45–60 min hands-on. **The second part is the workshop.**
- Groups of 5–6, from registration to Thursday's presentations
- Green sticky = following · Red sticky = stuck
- Errors are expected. Read them.
- The website stays online
